
The problem is that `isCelebrity(n, i)` has a precondition `requires n >= 0 && 0 <= i < n`. In the lemma `knowerCannotBeCelebrity`, the precondition is only `requires n >= 0`, but `isCelebrity(n, i)` requires `0 <= i < n`.

The counterexamples confirm this: i = -1, n = 39 (i < 0) and i = 8956, n = 1237 (i >= n).

The fix is to add `0 <= i < n` to the requires clause of the lemma.

This lemma has no loop, so it's not really about initiation or preservation. The issue is that the requires clause is insufficient to prove the ensures clause. This is closest to "bridge" - the precondition (requires) doesn't bridge to the postcondition (ensures).
